---
title: "Embed the Modules"
guide-section: "How-To"
---

The editor and viewer are Shiny Core modules, so you can place them in another app. This guide shows the smallest app that uses both, and the assets the page needs for the viewer to draw anything.

## Connect the editor to the viewer

Each module has a UI function and a server function. `editor_server()` returns the committed Mermaid code, and `viewer_server()` takes that value as its `code` argument:

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"18px", "darkMode":false}}}%%

flowchart TD
    subgraph UI["<strong>UI</strong>"]
        eui("<code>editor_ui('editor')</code>")
        vui("<code>viewer_ui('viewer')</code>")
    end
    subgraph Server["<strong>Server</strong>"]
        esrv("<code>editor_server('editor')</code>")
        code[/"<code>code</code><br>reactive.Value[str]"/]
        vsrv("<code>viewer_server('viewer', code=code)</code>")
    end
    eui -.-> esrv
    esrv --> code --> vsrv
    vui -.-> vsrv

    style UI fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10
    style Server fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10
    style eui fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
    style vui fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
    style esrv fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
    style vsrv fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
```

The dotted lines pair each UI function with its server function through a shared id. The solid line is the only data that crosses between the modules.

## Add the page assets

The viewer draws nothing on its own. The browser needs Mermaid, svg-pan-zoom, and the package's JavaScript binding, and the page needs the package stylesheet. The app below adds all four to the page head and serves the package's `www/` folder at `/shymermaid`:

```python
from pathlib import Path

import shymermaid
from shiny import App, ui

from shymermaid import editor_server, editor_ui, viewer_server, viewer_ui

WWW = Path(shymermaid.__file__).parent / "www"
MERMAID_JS = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.4.1/dist/mermaid.min.js"
PANZOOM_JS = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.2/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js"

app_ui = ui.page_fillable(
    ui.head_content(
        ui.tags.script(src=MERMAID_JS),
        ui.tags.script(src=PANZOOM_JS),
        ui.tags.link(rel="stylesheet", href="shymermaid/styles.css"),
        ui.tags.script(src="shymermaid/mermaid-binding.js"),
    ),
    ui.layout_sidebar(ui.sidebar(editor_ui("editor")), viewer_ui("viewer")),
)


def server(input, output, session):
    code = editor_server("editor")
    viewer_server("viewer", code=code)


app = App(app_ui, server, static_assets={"/shymermaid": WWW})
```

The script order matters. Mermaid and svg-pan-zoom must load before `mermaid-binding.js`, because the binding calls both libraries when the first diagram arrives.

::: {.callout-warning}
Without the `static_assets` argument, the stylesheet and binding return 404 errors. The page still loads, but the canvas stays empty and no error appears in the app.
:::

## Use your own code source

`viewer_server()` accepts any `reactive.Value[str]`, so the editor is optional. A fixed diagram, a file reader, or another module can supply the code instead:

```python
from shiny import reactive


def server(input, output, session):
    code = reactive.Value("flowchart TD\n    a --> b")
    viewer_server("viewer", code=code)
```

We can confirm it works by running the app and checking that the canvas shows the two node flowchart.

## Recap

Pass the value from `editor_server()` (or any `reactive.Value[str]`) to `viewer_server()`. Add the two libraries, the stylesheet, and the binding to the page head, and serve `www/` at `/shymermaid`. The [Render Cycle](02.02-explanation-render-cycle.qmd) page explains what happens to the code after it leaves Python.
